text.p: Italy sent home 180 Albanians, classified as "undesirables", just hours after they arrived on a boat packed with more than 1,000 refugees at the southern port of Bari, coastguards said on Monday.

A port official said the ageing tanker was carrying 1,229 Albanians, including many women and children, when it docked on Sunday. Most were sent to refugee centres around the country but some were immediately repatriated.

"Two boats with 180 undesirables have left for Albania this morning," a coastguard official said, adding that five of the ship's crew had been detained in Bari on charges of running a lucrative traffic in refugees.
Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano indicated that many more from this latest wave of Albanian immigrants to hit Italy might soon be sent packing.
"Yesterday there was a large arrival... of men, women and children that one might better call potential illegal immigrants," Napolitano said in a radio interview.
"We will carry out investigations, sending back those who have no evident need of protection or are not fleeing to Italy because of risk to their life," he added.

The tanker, the Irini, set sail from close to the northern Albanian city of Shkoder on Saturday and was intercepted in Italian waters on Sunday where coastguards tried in vain to persuade it to turn back.

Security sources in the Albanian capital Tirana said the boat had been bought in Montenegro for $120,000 by a gang based in northern Albania that was organising the traffic of illegal immigrants. The refugees said they paid around $500 each for the passage to Italy.
The Italian parliament voted in March to allow genuine refugees to stay a maximum of 90 days but to repatriate criminal elements and those simply looking for a better standard of life.

The Irini was the latest in a string of decrepit Albanian boats which have brought more than 13,000 people to Italy since the collapse of high-risk savings funds swept the Balkan country into anarchy earlier this year.
An estimated 103 people drowned on March 28 when an overcrowded ship from southern Albania collided with an Italian navy frigate and sank.

Napolitano said troops from a 6,000-strong Italian-led multinational force, sent last month to secure Albania's ports and roads and to protect the distribution of aid, were not yet present in the north to prevent illegal immigration.
"The multinational force...is not yet deployed along all the coast, especially not in Shkoder," he said.
Defence sources said on Sunday they thought thousands of Albanians were camped out near beaches in the north awaiting more ships to ferry them across the Adriatic to Italy.
